questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

If / it will rain, / we will have / a tough time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'it will rain'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'it rains' **should be used instead of** 'it will rain'.**
 
• The sentence is **a conditional statement.** In conditional sentences of this structure (**first conditional**), the correct order is: *"If + present simple, will + base verb." *The original sentence, *"If it will rain, we will have a tough time," *creates a redundancy by using "**will**" after "**if**."
 
• In English, it's incorrect to use "will" in both parts of** a conditional sentence.** Instead, the structure should have*** "if + present simple"*** in the conditional clause. So, the correct arrangement should be: *"If it rains, we will have a tough time." *

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *If **it rains**, we will have a tough time.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Does Sneha not lick the butter?

options.text: Is the butter being licked by Sneha?
Is the butter not licked by Sneha?
Sneha does not lick the butter?
Was Sneha not licking the butter?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Is the butter not licked by Sneha?'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is written in an interrogative form as the question tag is there, and we need to convert it into** the passive form.**
 
• Active Voice describes a sentence where the subject performs the action stated by the **verb**. While in the Passive Voice subject is acted upon by the **verb**.
 
• We follow the following structure in case of an interrogative sentence:
 
 
• Active voice: Do/Does/Did + Doer + Verb 1 + Noun/Pronoun + Rest of the sentence__
 __
 
• Example - *Do they beat you every day? (Active)*
 
 
 
• Passive voice: Am/is/are/was/were + Noun/Pronoun + Verb 3 + By + Doer + Rest of the sentence__
 __
 
• Example - *Are you beaten by them every day? (Passive)*
 
 
 
 

 
• While converting Interrogative Active into Interrogative Passive Voice.

 
 
• The** helping verb** comes before the object in the passive voice, (as the **passive voice** starts with the object of the **active voice**)
 
• Convert the verb into** past participle **or **3rd form of the verb.**
 
• Use the preposition ‘**by**’.
 
• Complete the sentence with the **subject** and sign of Interrogation (?).
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 2.**

 

Correct Passive form__: *Is the butter not licked by Sneha?*

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.**

Cut corners

options.text: He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.
The artist cut corners on the painting, and it ended up looking unfinished.
I always make sure to cut corners when I'm driving to save time.
I cut corners to finish my project on time, and my boss praised me for my hard work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence that uses the idiom **"cut corners" **correctly is:* He cut corners on his homework and got a bad grade.*
 
• The idiom **"cut corners" **refers to doing something hastily or in a way that compromises quality by neglecting necessary steps or standards. In this sentence, it implies that the person didn't put in the required effort or complete the homework properly, leading to a bad grade.
 
 
• *Example sentence: "She **cut corners** while preparing the report, so it lacked crucial information."*
 
 
 
• It's possible that in the context of the idiom's meaning, the first sentence illustrates the concept of** "cutting corners"** more accurately by implying that the poor quality or outcome (the bad grade) resulted from not properly completing the homework.

 

**Correct Answer:__** *He** cut corners **on his homework and got a bad grade.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin: **

 
 
• **​**The origin of the idiom **"cut corners"** possibly comes from **the idea of literally cutting the corners** of a shape or object to save time or resources.
 
• In various tasks or activities, skipping corners, which represent essential steps or details, leads to an incomplete or inadequate result.
 
• This phrase has been figuratively extended to denote doing something hastily or with less attention to quality.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Rover would not swallow the pill.

options.text: The pill would not be swallowing by Rover.
The pill would not swallowed by Rover.
The pill would not be swallowed by Rover.
The pill would not be swallow by Rover.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The pill would not be swallowed by Rover.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of** Active Voice. **As per the given question, we have to change it to **Passive Voice.** 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is **'Rover'. **
 
• The object of the given sentence is** 'the pill'. **
 
• Since a modal verb has been used in the active voice, therefore, the passive voice will follow the given structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice - Subject + **modal verb*(would) *+ V1 + Object.**
 
• Passive Voice - Object(Subjective form) **modal verb*(would)* + be + V3 Subject (Objective form).**
 
 
 
• Here, **'would not swallow' **is changed into **'would not be swallowed'** because in** the 'active to passive' **transformation third form of the verb is used. 
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the above-mentioned points, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *The pill would not be swallowed by Rover.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.**

The moon is Earth's only natural satellite and __the nearby large__ celestial body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'the nearest large'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence aims to describe the **moon** in terms of its proximity **to Earth and its significant size compared **to other celestial bodies.
 
• The original phrase **"nearby large"** doesn't effectively convey both the sense of proximity and the notion of significant size.
 
• The corrected phrase** "the nearest large" **effectively combines two elements:
 
 
• "**Nearest**" indicates the proximity of the moon to Earth, portraying it as the closest celestial body.
 
• "**Large**" denotes the substantial size of the moon among other celestial bodies, indicating its importance or significant dimensions.
 
 
 
• Grammatically, "**nearest**" functions as** a superlative form** of "**near**," signifying the closest in distance. It modifies "**large**," emphasizing that among the celestial bodies in proximity to Earth, the moon is not only close but also substantial in size compared to others.
 
• So, the chosen option,*** "the nearest large," ***effectively communicates both the idea of proximity and the significance of size in a grammatically correct manner, making it the most suitable substitution. 

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The moon is Earth's only natural satellite and **the nearest large** celestial body.*
